round1.reply:
Support-it

P1: The four-entry hostile-input list fits the card 226 gap: F1 and F2 were reached only at review, and the proposal moves that check into the slice and red.
P2: The architect writes the line and the red seat answers it in its own commit body, so each role stays in its own context.
P3: The reviewer checks the red body first, and "n/a" without a reason counts as not run, so the check can be audited.
P4: "No list input" and no new file, seat or meeting keep it light and avoid over-specifying (VISION.md ruling 6).
P5: It is kept apart from D157, D158, D165 and D166, with its own metric, so credit isn't blurred.
P6: The metric is input-gap review findings per card (target 0), with a stated baseline of 2, plus counter-metrics for ceremony cost.
P7: It is a two-way door, scoped to 3 cards, and keep, revise or drop is decided at the retro, so removal waits for the retro.
P8: The git-visible accountability check lets the auditor tick FAIL a card that skips it, which fits "open FAILs stop the line".

Yes

P1: C1 is sound and minimal. One fixed four-entry line is easy to check, and "n/a: <reason>" avoids forcing fake cases.
P2: C2 is enforceable. A test name that exists in that red can be checked mechanically from git.
P3: C3 is clear. A missing name or a reasonless n/a counts as "not run", so a reviewer can apply it without judgment calls.
P4: C4 is fine. "no list input" gives a clean exit, and there is no new file, seat or checker, so no checker false positives are possible.
P5: C5 keeps the boundaries with D157, D158, D165 and D166 clear. The "first rule to name it gets the catch" tie-break prevents double credit.
P6: The metric, baseline and scope are measurable from the review record. The trial is capped at 3 cards and is a two-way door.

P4 (C4, "no list input"): Fine. A one-phrase opt-out keeps ceremony off the other cards.
P5 (C5, no blur with D157, D158, D165 and D166): Fine. Each rule keeps its own metric and nothing moves into the green.
